summary: Formalized architectural governance by integrating structural integrity frameworks (PEP 487, DAG-based knowledge modeling) with proactive maintenance mechanisms like Semantic Cache Decay, Reflective Achievement Audits, and AST-based rationale enforcement. This evolution shifts the system from reactive task execution to high-signal, proactive architectural hardening, ensuring long-term reliability and cognitive sustainability.
key_learnings: PEP 487 and structural hashing provide robust defense against state-space ambiguity.
Representing knowledge as a DAG prevents cognitive overload by enforcing foundational mastery.
Token consumption and decorator-based middleware are essential for granular LLM observability.
Stability and architectural integrity are prerequisites for long-term velocity.
Linking cache TTL to knowledge review cycles prevents stale data retrieval.
Enforcing architectural intent via AST-based validation is more efficient than reactive auditing.
Semantic consolidation and formal reflection phases are critical to eliminating technical debt.
